# Stacks & Queues in Lua

Lua has exactly one data structure — the **table** — and it is enough. A stack is a table plus `push`/`pop` at the end; a queue is a table plus two moving indices (a **ring buffer** if you wrap them).

Lua cells run fully offline via Wasmoon, and like C/Rust cells they publish values to the notebook by printing `__NB_SET__` marker lines.

-- A stack is just a table used from one end.
local Stack = {}
Stack.__index = Stack

function Stack.new()
  return setmetatable({ items = {}, top = 0 }, Stack)
end

function Stack:push(v)
  self.top = self.top + 1
  self.items[self.top] = v
end

function Stack:pop()
  if self.top == 0 then return nil end
  local v = self.items[self.top]
  self.items[self.top] = nil
  self.top = self.top - 1
  return v
end

-- Classic stack job: are the brackets balanced?
local pairs_map = { [")"] = "(", ["]"] = "[", ["}"] = "{" }

local function balanced(s)
  local st = Stack.new()
  for i = 1, #s do
    local ch = s:sub(i, i)
    if ch == "(" or ch == "[" or ch == "{" then
      st:push(ch)
    elseif pairs_map[ch] then
      if st:pop() ~= pairs_map[ch] then return false end
    end
  end
  return st.top == 0
end

local tests = {
  "(a[b]{c})",
  "([)]",
  "function f() return {1, 2} end",
  "if (x[1] > 0 then",
  "{{[[(())]]}}",
}

local results = {}
for _, s in ipairs(tests) do
  local ok = balanced(s)
  results[#results + 1] = '{"text":"' .. s:gsub('"', '\\"') .. '","ok":' .. tostring(ok) .. '}'
  print(string.format("%-36s %s", s, ok and "balanced" or "NOT balanced"))
end

print('__NB_SET__ {"key":"bracket_results","value":[' .. table.concat(results, ",") .. ']}')

## A queue that never shuffles

Naive queues `table.remove(t, 1)` — which shifts every element, O(n) per pop. The ring buffer below keeps a `first` and `last` index instead, so both ends are O(1).

local Queue = {}
Queue.__index = Queue

function Queue.new()
  return setmetatable({ items = {}, first = 1, last = 0 }, Queue)
end

function Queue:enqueue(v)
  self.last = self.last + 1
  self.items[self.last] = v
end

function Queue:dequeue()
  if self.first > self.last then return nil end
  local v = self.items[self.first]
  self.items[self.first] = nil
  self.first = self.first + 1
  return v
end

function Queue:size()
  return self.last - self.first + 1
end

-- A print spooler: jobs arrive with page counts; the printer does
-- 5 pages per tick, requeueing unfinished jobs (round-robin).
local q = Queue.new()
local jobs = {
  { name = "thesis.pdf",   pages = 12 },
  { name = "photo.png",    pages = 2 },
  { name = "report.docx",  pages = 7 },
  { name = "ticket.pdf",   pages = 1 },
}
for _, j in ipairs(jobs) do q:enqueue(j) end

local tick = 0
local finished = {}
while q:size() > 0 do
  tick = tick + 1
  local job = q:dequeue()
  local printed = math.min(5, job.pages)
  job.pages = job.pages - printed
  if job.pages > 0 then
    print(string.format("tick %d: %-12s printed %d, %d left -> back of queue", tick, job.name, printed, job.pages))
    q:enqueue(job)
  else
    print(string.format("tick %d: %-12s printed %d, DONE", tick, job.name, printed))
    finished[#finished + 1] = '"' .. job.name .. '"'
  end
end

print('__NB_SET__ {"key":"spool_order","value":[' .. table.concat(finished, ",") .. ']}')

## Try this

- Give the spooler a **priority lane**: two queues, urgent jobs drain first. Which structure from this notebook would you reuse?
- Make `balanced` report *where* the mismatch happened (character index).
- Change the printer speed from 5 to 1 page per tick — does the completion order change? Why (round-robin fairness)?
